## Vocabulary

- **self**: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads (16/5)

## Structure and components

- [statement] A 2019 engineering account describes reducing three MongoDB collections from individually provisioned throughput to shared database throughput, then encountering shard-key requirements and import throttling. Its practical lesson is to test collection layout and migration traffic as part of sizing; its historical minimum-throughput figures should not be reused as current prices. (low confidence) — https://benc.dev/blog/cosmos-sharding/ · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads

## How it works

- [statement] Inspect explain execution statistics when a query is expensive: compare retrievedDocumentCount with outputDocumentCount, inspect pathsNotIndexed, and inspect shardInformation. Microsoft documents partition-key equality filters as reducing query fan-out and RU consumption. A historical count-query trace demonstrates that an indexed-looking query can still retrieve many documents and incur high RU. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/troubleshoot-query-performance · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://gist.github.com/extrawurst/6385e793a841111a6f81c71f18be1edf, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/find-request-unit-charge
- [statement] Adiom recommends testing query and write performance under expected load and reviewing indexes when moving between MongoDB-compatible implementations. Microsoft likewise documents MongoDB-API-specific indexing behavior and distinguishes RU-reducing changes from latency-only changes; do not assume an Atlas query plan transfers unchanged. (medium confidence) — https://adiom.io/post/migrate-from-cosmos-db-ru-for-mongodb-vcore-or-atlas · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/troubleshoot-query-performance

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Run db.runCommand({getLastRequestStatistics: 1}) after the operation under examination to retrieve its command name, request charge and duration. The portal Query Stats view covers query predicates; use a shell or driver command for data manipulation operations. (medium confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/find-request-unit-charge · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://gist.github.com/extrawurst/6385e793a841111a6f81c71f18be1edf
- [statement] Use the measured workload mix to estimate RU/s: sum each operation class's measured RU charge multiplied by its operations per second. This is a planning inference from Microsoft's operation-rate estimator and throughput example, not a guarantee against partition-local throttling. Validate the resulting capacity with representative load. (medium confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/estimate-ru-capacity-planner · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/troubleshoot-query-performance

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Adiom's February 28, 2025 migration article reports that scan-heavy workloads and large ingestion jobs can require substantial RU provisioning, and that teams may overprovision to avoid performance issues. Treat this as a migration vendor's qualitative experience, not an independent quantified Atlas-versus-Cosmos TCO result. (low confidence) — https://adiom.io/post/migrate-from-cosmos-db-ru-for-mongodb-vcore-or-atlas · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] The estimator's July 21, 2026 documentation describes a public-preview estimate rather than a quote. Model document sizes, operation rates, capacity mode, storage, region count, backup and discounts explicitly, and export the configuration so a competitor cost comparison can be reproduced. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-21) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/estimate-ru-capacity-planner · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] RUs normalize the resources consumed by database operations; RU/s expresses throughput capacity. Size MongoDB workloads from operation rates and measured request charges rather than equating one database operation with one RU. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/find-request-unit-charge · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/estimate-ru-capacity-planner
- [statement] The MongoDB Cost Estimator maps find to Reads, insert to Writes, update to Updates, delete to Deletes, and aggregate/query to Queries. It accepts document sizes and operation rates plus capacity, region and pricing settings; its projected cost is an estimate rather than a quote. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-21) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/estimate-ru-capacity-planner · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Scope the comparison to RU-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB. PowerSync identifies RU-based Cosmos and the vCore/Azure DocumentDB engine as distinct offerings; an RU capacity estimate must not be treated as a vCore cluster quote. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/powersync-ja/powersync-service/blob/main/docs/documentdb/documentdb-limitations.md · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://adiom.io/post/migrate-from-cosmos-db-ru-for-mongodb-vcore-or-atlas
- [statement] For workload sizing, measure request charge on representative MongoDB operations before projecting throughput. RU abstracts CPU, I/O and memory consumption; it is not a fixed price per MongoDB command. Microsoft recommends obtaining query RU charge before optimization. (high confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/find-request-unit-charge · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/troubleshoot-query-performance
- [statement] The MongoDB estimator maps find to Reads, insert to Writes, update to Updates, delete to Deletes, and aggregate/query to Queries. Its documented simple/filter/complex query hints are approximately 3/10/30 RU; these are calculator assumptions, not measured charges for arbitrary MongoDB queries. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-21) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/estimate-ru-capacity-planner · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] Microsoft gives Provisioned RU/s = C*T/R as a rough starting estimate, with C=1000 RU/s per vCore for Cosmos DB for MongoDB v4.0, T the total cores across data-bearing replicas, and R the replication factor. Exclude routing/configuration cores; check whether a managed service reports cores per replica before calculating T. This is not a version-independent benchmark or guaranteed equivalence. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-27) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/convert-vcore-to-request-unit · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] In an August 22, 2020 user trace, a filtered count returning 29,239 recorded RequestCharge=1290.15; explain reported 29,283 retrieved documents and indexHitRatio=0 despite listed indexes. This is a reproducible-looking historical diagnostic artifact, not a current cost benchmark or proof that every count query behaves this way. (low confidence) — https://gist.github.com/extrawurst/6385e793a841111a6f81c71f18be1edf · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] Query partition targeting affects RU demand: an equality filter on the partition key limits index work to the relevant partition, whereas indexed cross-partition queries still execute independently on multiple partitions. Include actual shard-key access patterns in the estimate. (low confidence) — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/mongodb/troubleshoot-query-performance · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads
- [statement] Budget bulk ingestion separately from steady-state traffic and validate it under load. Adiom identifies large ingestion and scan-heavy workloads as provisioning risks; an independent MongoDB-API demo account reported import throttling at its low steady-state allocation and successful import after a temporary increase. These accounts do not supply a universal RU-per-write constant. (medium confidence) — https://adiom.io/post/migrate-from-cosmos-db-ru-for-mongodb-vcore-or-atlas · keywords: Cosmos DB RU estimation for MongoDB workloads · also: https://benc.dev/blog/cosmos-sharding/
